bull_case: Better monetization of the installed consumer/merchant network can restore durable growth without requiring major share gains.
bear_case: Platform wallets and merchant-native checkout can continue eroding branded relevance at the margin.
thesis: PayPal remains structurally relevant because digital payments keep expanding and its two-sided network is extremely large. Leadership is durable but no longer category-defining in every checkout surface.

evidence.claim: FY2025 active accounts were 439M and TPV $1.79T.
PayPal operates branded checkout, Venmo, Braintree, BNPL and merchant services across roughly 200 markets.

counterevidence: Branded checkout competition remains intense and active-account growth is essentially flat, limiting evidence of a widening moat.
falsifiers: If transaction-margin dollars contract persistently, branded checkout resumes material share loss, or buybacks stop creating FCF/share growth, the thesis weakens.

key_kpis.name: owner FCF/share
key_kpis.threshold: sustained growth despite modest revenue growth

next_checks: Branded checkout growth, Venmo revenue, transaction-margin dollars, active accounts, TPV, repurchases, diluted shares

subscores.rationale: Digital payments and commerce continue secular growth, though wallet competition is mature.
PayPal/Venmo remain globally recognized consumer-payment brands with very large merchant distribution.
Branded checkout, Venmo, Braintree and financial services create multiple demand axes, offset by intense platform competition.

uncertainties.rationale: Payments competition and transformation execution remain the primary uncertainty.
